newsitem.title: UK: Smith & Nephew trials of Dermagraft a success.
newsitem.headline: Smith & Nephew trials of Dermagraft a success.

text.p: Healthcare group Smith & Nephew Plc and California-based Advanced Tissue Sciences said on Monday the pivotal clinical trial of Dermagraft treatment for diabetic foot ulcers had been completed successfully.
Dermagraft is the first product of the joint venture between the two companies announced earlier this year.
Smith & Nephew said in a statement that results of the trial "demonstrated a statistically highly significant improvement" in how quickly patients treated with Dermagraft healed.
Smith & Nephew said details of the full clinical trials were expected to be presented at the Advanced Wound Care Symposium in New Orleans in April 1997.
It said Dermagraft gave improvements in both the percentage of wounds healed and the time to complete healing.
The company said it planned to submit a premarket approval (PMA) application to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in December this year.
The FDA has already agreed to deal with such an application on an expedited reveiw basis.
Smith & Nephew chief executive John Robinson said the companies were preparing for a potential launch in the U.S. and the UK during the second half of 1997 with roll-out continuing during 1998.
